title: Discount threshold uses > instead of >=
reasoning: The promo policy states '10% off orders of $100.00 or more', which is an inclusive lower bound. The implementation in apply_discount uses a strict greater-than comparison (amount > DISCOUNT_THRESHOLD), which excludes the exact boundary value $100.00. When a customer's cart totals exactly $100.00 the condition evaluates to False and no discount is applied, matching the log line discount_applied=false and the CI failure. Carts above $100.00 (e.g. $120.00) satisfy the strict inequality and correctly receive the discount.
evidence: $120.00 cart gets discount but $100.00 cart does not
CI: AssertionError: assert Decimal('100.00') == Decimal('90.00') for test_discount_applies_at_exactly_100
pricing.py line 30: `if amount > DISCOUNT_THRESHOLD:` — strict > excludes the boundary
